דאב.def:
H1669. daeb

[דָּאֵב‎] verb become faint, languish (Late Hebrew id. Hiph`il; compare Arabic toil, weary oneself; see also דְּאָבוֺן דְּאָבָה,‎ & compare דוב‎) —

Qal Perfect3feminine singular דָּֽאֲבָה‎ Psa 88:10 (subject עַיִן‎); Infinitive לְדַאֲבָה‎ Jer 31:12 לְד יוֺסִיפוּ ׳לֹא‎ (subject ransomed Israel); — 31:25 has דָּֽאֲבָה נֶפֶשׁ‎, of hunger (|| עֲיֵפָ֑ה נֶפֶשׁ‎), where adjective or participle seems needed; Hi Gf דְּאֵבָה‎ or דֹּאֲבָה‎ (the punctuators had, according to them, the Aramaic participle in mind); Thes. makes relative clause.

דאבון.def:
H1671. deabon

[דְּאָבוֺן‎] noun [masculine] faintness, languishing, construct נָ֑פֶשׁ וְַדאֲבוֺן עֵינַיִם וְכִלְיוֺן‎ Deut 28:65 (compare Lev 26:16 & Syriac see דוב‎).

דאג.def:
ו‎

ו‎, Waw, sixth letter; in modern Hebrew = numeral 6; no evidence of this usage in OT times.

וָ וּ, וְ,‎

demonstrative adverb and

conjunction so, then, and (Phoenician, Moabite, Aramaic ו‎; Arabic ; Ethiopic Assyrian u DlW (but between verbs the usually connective is the enclitic ma KAT2. 508, Dl§§ 82, 150). The use in Hebrew shews that original וְ‎ was not a merely copulative conjunction, but that it possessed a demonstrative force (compare Dr§ 122), which is often perceptible as such, though in other cases, from its being applied to denote mere juxtaposition or connection [compare Greek τε, and Latin tum .... tum = 'both .... and,' both properly demonstratives: Assyrian ma has also a demonstrative force, Dl§ 79], it is less palpable) — וְ‎ before shwa' mobile or a labial is vocalized וּ‎; often before a tone-syll., when the word itself has a disj. accent, וָ‎ (as וַָמתִּי׃‎ Gen 19:19; וָמֵ֖תוּ‎ 33:13; וָמֵ֑ת‎ 44:9; וָחָֽיָה׃‎ Exod 1:16; וָיָ֑מָּה‎ Josh 15:46; וָ֔לֹ֕א‎ 2Sam 13:26; וָאָ֖רֶץ‎ Isa 26:19; וָקָ֔מוּ‎ 49:7; וָחָֽתָּה׃‎ Jer 48:1; וָרָֹע‎ Psa 10:15); especially when it forms with the preceding word a pair, whether of parallel or opposed ideas (as וָכֹה כֹּה‎ Exod 2:12, וָמִ֖י מִי‎ 10:8, וָאָ֑בֶן אֶבֶן‎ Deut 25:13; וָדֹ֑ר דֹּר‎ 32:7 +; וָבֹ֔הוּ תֹּהוּ‎ Gen 1:2, וָרֶמֶ֛שׂ בְּהֵמָה‎ 1:24, וָרָֽע׃ טוֺב‎ 2:19, וָנָ֖ד נָע‎ 4:12, וָלָ֖יְלָה וְיוֺם וָחֹ֛רֶף וְקַיִץ‎ 8:22, וֵָלךְ׃ קַח‎ 12:19, וָאָֽרֶץ׃ שָׁמַיִם‎ 14:19, וָאָ֑תָּה אֲנִי‎ 31:44, וָה֑וּא אֲנִי‎ 41:11, וָשׁוּבוּ עִבְרוּ‎ Exod 32:27, וָהֵ֛ם אַתָּה‎ Num 16:16, וָמֶ֑לָךְ אֱלֹהִים‎ 1Kin 21:13, וָנֶ֖כֶד נִין‎ Isa 14:22, וָשֶׁ֖בֶר שֹׁד‎ 59:7; and often: see more fully Bö§ 600); occasionally also with a conjunctive accent (as לְעֹלָֽם׃ וָשַחי‎ Gen 3:22 compare Lev 18:5, שָׁם וָמַ֣תְנוּ‎ 2Kin 7:4, חֲדָשָׁ֑ה וָאָ֣רֶץ‎ Isa 65:17; Prov 25:3, גָּדוֺל׃ וָשֶשׁבֶר שֹׁ֖ד‎ Jer 48:3, compare 32:29). — וְ‎ is used very freely and widely in Hebrew, but also with much delicacy, to express relations and shades of meaning which Western languages would usually indicate by distinct particles. But in Hebrew particles such as לָכֵן לְמַעַן, בַּעֲבוּר, אוּלָם, אָכֵן, אַךְ, אָז, אוֺ,‎, etc., were reserved for cases in which special emphasis or distinctness was desired: their frequent use was felt instinctively to be inconsistent with the lightness and grace of movement which the Hebrew ear loved; and thus in AV, RV, words like or, then, but, notwithstanding, howbeit, so, thus, therefore, that, constantly appear, where the Hebrew has simply וְ‎.

1 And, connecting both words (see above), and sentences (Gen 1:5 וג קָרָא ׳וְלַחשֶׁךְ‎). When three, four, or more words follow, the conjunction may connect them all, as 7:21; 10:2 (6 t.) 24:35 (7 t.) Josh 7:24 (10 t.) 2Sam 17:28f.: often however it is prefixed only to the last, as Gen 5:32; 10:1; Deut 18:10 etc.; occas. even it connects only the first two, 1Kin 8:47; Isa 1:13; Psa 45:9; Job 42:9. Remarkably, however, וְ‎ as a mere conjunction is, as a rule, not in classical Hebrew attached directly to verbs (especially in the perfect), the construction with וְ‎ consecutive (see

2) being (as in Moabite) preferred: thus וַיִּבֶן יָצָא‎ is said, not וּבָנָה יָצָא‎. Exceptions in classical Hebrew are (a) sometimes where synonyms are coupled, as Num 23:19 וְדִבֶּר ֗֗֗ אָמַר‎, Deut 2:30; Judg 5:26; 1Sam 12:2; Isa 1:2 ורוממתי גדּלתי‎ 2:11; 5:14; 8:8; 19:6; 29:20; (b) isolated cases, difficult to reduce to rule (perhaps sometimes due to textual error), as Gen 28:6; 38:5; Judg 3:23; 7:13; 16:18; 1Sam 1:12; 3:13; 4:19; 5:7; 10:9; 17:38, 48; 25:20 and elsewhere (in other passages, apparently similar, the perfect and וְ‎ has a frequent. force (see 2), as Gen 37:3; Exod 36:29f.; Num 10:17f. 21:15, 20; 1Sam 2:22; 16:14; 17:34f. (see Dr) 27:9; 2Sam 16:13; 17:17, perhaps also Gen 15:6; 21:25; 34:5). In later parts of OT, probably through Aramaic influence, the perfect with simple וְ‎ occurs more frequently: so especially in Ecclesiastes, where it is all but universal (e.g. 2:11-12, 13, 15 etc.). With the imperfect, the simple וְ‎ is not so unidiomatic, even in classical Hebrew (compare 3); see 1:9, 26; 9:27; 17:2; 22:17; 27:29; Exod 23:8 (frequently) 24:7; Num 14:12; Deut 17:13; 30:12-13, Josh 3:13; 7:3; Judg 7:3; 13:8; Isa 5:29; 14:10; often also in Jeremiah, Isa2, Job, Psalms, e.g. 40:30; 41:20 (Dr§ 116: contrast 28:13). See more fully Dr§ 130-4 Ges§ 112. 6. Special senses: —

a. it sometimes = and specially, Gen 3:16; 1Kin 11:1 many strange women, and specially the daughter of Pharaoh, Isa 1:1 Judah and (= and particularly) Jerusalem, 2:1; 9:7; Psa 18:1.

b. and in particular ('und zwar'), and that (explicative), Gen 4:4; Judg 7:22; 1Sam 17:40 וּבַיַּלְקוּט‎, 28:3 in Ramah, and that in his city (unusual: text suspicious), 2Sam 13:20 וְשֹׁמֵמָה‎ and that desolate, Isa 57:11 I have been silent וּמֵעוֺלָם‎ and that from of old, 32:7; Jer 15:13; Amos 3:11 (si vera lectio), 4:10; Zech 9:9b Mal 1:11; Psa 68:10; Prov 3:12; Lam 3:26; Eccl 8:2; Dan 1:3; 8:10; 9:25, 27; Neh 8:13; 1Chr 9:27; 2Chr 8:13; 29:27 (but' even' for ו‎, before ל‎ and infinitive, e.g. in Isa 44:28; Jer 17:10; 19:12, is wrong; see Ew§ 351 c, Dr§ 206).

c. sometimes it introduces an idea which so exceeds or adds to what has preceded, that it is nearly equivalent to also, 1Sam 25:43; 1Kin 2:22 ask also the kingdom for him; unusually Hosea 8:6 והוא מישׂראל כי‎ for of Israel is it also, Eccl 5:6 והבלים‎ (see De) 2Chr 27:5 (but see ᵐ5‎). Or it may be rendered yea: so especially in the ascending numerations 3-4 Amos 1:3, 6, 9, 11, 13; 2:1, 4, 6; Prov 30:18, 21, 29, 6-7 6:16; Job 5:19, 7-8 Micah 5:4 — the first number being aggravated, or augmented, by a higher. In one idiom וּגְבוּל‎, occurring in geographic descriptions, it is used peculiarly, seemingly = at the same time: Num 34:6 and as for the western border, וּגְבוּל הַגָּדוֺל הַיָּם לָכֶם וְהָיָה‎ the great sea shall be to you also (German 'zugleich') a border, Deut 3:16 וּגְבוּל הַנַּחַל תּוֺךְ‎ the middle of the stream being at the same time the border, 3:17; Josh 13:23, 27; 15:12, 47 (but these, except Num 34:6, might be cases of 5c γ).

d. it connects alternative cases, so that it = or: Exod 20:10, 17; 21:16 he that stealeth a man בְיָדוֺ וְנִמְצָא וּמְכָרוֺ‎ and selleth him, and (= or if) he be found in his hand, 21:17; Lev 21:14; 22:23-24, Prov 29:9 (Fl Ew RV: whether . . . or) Job 31:13, 16, 26, etc.

e. it connects contrasted ideas, where in our idiom the contrast would be expressed explicitly by but; in such cases prominence is usually given to the contrasted idea by its being placed immediately after the conjunction: Gen 2:17 but of the tree of the knowledge . . . thou shalt not eat, 4:2, 5; 6:8; 17:21; 31:10 etc., 1Kin 2:26; 10:7; 11:32, 34; 15:14; Prov 10:1-2, 3, 4 + often; even after לֹא‎ (where כִּי‎ or אִם כִּי‎ might be expected), as Gen 42:10; Exod 21:18; Lev 26:45; Deut 11:11; Judg 19:12; 1Kin 3:11.

f. it introduces a contrasted idea in such a way as to suggest a question, especially before a pronoun, Judg 14:16 I told it not to my father or my mother, אַגִּיד וְלָךְ‎ and shall I told it unto thee? 2Sam 11:11; Jer 25:29 תִנָּקוּ הִנָּקֵה וְאַתֶּם‎ and shall ye be guiltless? 45:5; Ezek 20:31; 33:25b Jonah 4:11. So the וְ‎ consecutive and perfect (see 2a), Exod 5:5 וְהִשְׁבַּתֶּם‎ and will ye make them rest from their burdens? Num 16:10 וּבִקַּשְׁתֶּם‎ and seek ye the priesthood also? 1Sam 25:11; Isa 66:9; Psa 50:21 and shall I keep silence? Job 32:16 (compare Dr§ 119 γ).

g. attaching a fresh subj. (or object) to a clause already grammatically complete, it = and also, Gen 2:9b Num 16:2, 18 and they stood at the entrance of the tent of meeting, ואהרן ומשׁה‎ and Moses and Aaron (stood also), 16:27; Exod 35:22; Judg 6:5; Gen 1:16; b 12:17; 44:2; 46:15; Exod 29:3; Jer 32:29 (compare DrSm. i. 6, 11, & p. 293): when the idea thus attached is subordinate, or not logically embraced in the principal predicate, it approximates to the Arabic or 'waw of association' (followed by an accusative: WAG ii. § 37), Est 4:16 אָצוּם וְנַעֲרֹתַי אֲנִי‎ I will fast (singular) and (= with) my maidens, Exod 21:4; 1Sam 25:42; 29:10b (but insert here אַתָּה‎ with ᵐ5‎) 2Sam 12:30 (but read וּבָהּ‎, as 1Chr 20:2) 1Sam 20:10; Neh 6:12; Gen 4:20; Isa 42:5; Jer 19:1 (but read מזקני וְלָקַחְתָּ֫‎ with ᵐ5‎) 2Chr 2:3; 13:11; compare Jer 22:7 (וְכֵלָיו אִישׁ‎), Job 41:12. Whether Isa 48:16 וְרוּחוֺ‎ belongs here, is dubious

h. וְ‎ repeated = both . . . and (but גַּם ֗֗֗ גַּם‎) is more usual in this sense); Gen 34:28; Num 9:14; Josh 9:23; 2Sam 5:8 (text dubious), Isa 16:5; 38:15; Jer 13:14; 21:6; 32:14 (text dubious) 32:20; 40:8; Psa 76:7; Job 34:29; Dan 8:13; Neh 12:28.

i. a repetition of the same word with וְ‎ interposed expresses (a) diversity (rare), Deut 25:13 וָאֶבֶן אֶבֶן‎ a weight and a weight, i.e. different weights (explained by וּקְטַנָּה גְּדֹלָה‎), 25:14; Prov 20:23; Psa 12:3 וָלֵב בְּלֵב‎ with a heart and a heart = with a double heart, 1Chr 12:33 וָלֵב לֵב בְּלֹא‎; (b) distribution (except in וָדֹר דֹּר‎ Deut 32:7; Isa 13:20 +?Intr. 505) Psa 87:5; 1Chr 26:13 וָשָֽׁעַר׃ לְשַׁעַר‎ = for every gate, 28:14 (twice in verse); 2Chr 8:14; 34:13; 35:15; Ezra 10:14 וָעִיר עִיר זִקְנֵי‎ elders of every city, Neh 13:24; Est 1:8, 22 (twice in verse); 2:12; 3:4, 12 (4 t. in verse); 8:9 (twice in verse); strengthened by כָּלֿ‎2Chr 11:12 ועיר עיר בכל‎ in every several city, 19:5; 28:25; 31:19; 32:28; Est 2:11 ויום בכליֿום‎, 3:14; 4:3; 8:11, 13, 17 (twice in verse); 9:21, 27, 28; Psalm 45:18; Psa 145:13 (common in post-Biblical Hebrew, especially with כל‎).

j. it is used in the formulation of proverbs (the Vav adaequationis, הִשְׁתַּוָּאָה וָו‎) as Prov 17:3; 25:3, 20, 25 cold waters to a thirsty soul and good news from a far country (i.e. they are like each other), 26:3, 9, 14, 20; 27:21; Eccl 5:2; 7:1; 8:8; compare 9:11; Psa 19:5; 125:2; Job 14:11f.; 14:19 (compare in Arabic 'every man and his cares [accusative],' 'every thing and its price,' i.e. they go together: 'merchants and dogs [accusative] of Seleucia,' i.e. they are like one another: see FlKl. Schr. iii. 535 f.). More rarely in the opposite order, 5:7; 12:11. But 1Sam 12:15b cannot be thus explained: read with וּבְמַלְכְּכֶם ᵐ5‎, and see Dr.

k. in circumstantial clauses וְ‎ introduces a statement of the concomitant conditions under which the action denoted by the principal verb takes place: in such cases, the relation expressed by וְ‎ must often in English be stated explicitly by a conjunction, as when, since, seeing, though, etc., as occasion may require. So very often, as Gen 11:4 let us build a tower בַשָּׁמַיִם וְראֹשׁוֺ‎ and its top in the heavens (= with its top in etc.), 18:12 shall I have pleasure, זָקֵן וַאדֹנִי‎ and my lord is old (= my lord being old)? Judg 16:15 How sayest thou, I love thee, אִתִּי אֵין וְלִבְּךָ‎ and (= when) thy heart is not with me? and especially with a person pronoun, Gen 15:2 what wilt thou give me עֲרִירִי הֹלֵךְ וְאָנֹכִי‎ and I (= the case being that I) am going hence childless? 18:13; 20:3 lo, thou wilt die because of the woman thou hast taken בָּֽעַל׃ בְּעֻלַת וְהִוא‎ = seeing she is married, 24:62 ישֵׁב וְהוּא‎ = since or for he was dwelling (different from וַיֵּשֶׁב‎ = and he proceeded to dwell), 26:27 וְאַתֶּם‎ seeing ye hate me, Judg 13:9 and came to her ישֶׁבֶת וְהִיא‎ = as she was sitting, 1Sam 18:23; 1Kin 19:19 +? Psa 72:12 the afflicted לוֺ וְאֵיןעֹֿזֵר‎ and (= when) he has no helper (compare Job 29:12), Job 104:25 מִסְמָּר וְאֵין‎, Job 105:34; 5:9. See more fully Dr§ 156-60 Ges§ 141, R 2. (The analogous use of the is very common in Arabic: Wii. § 183.) Introducing an appeal to a fact confirmatory of some statement or promise, it almost = as truly as (compare Ew§ 340 c) Hosea 12:6 and J. is God of hosts, J. is his name! Joel 4:20; Amos 9:5-6 Isa 51:15 and I [who promise this] am J. thy God, who . . . . ! Jer 29:23; Psa 89:38b (compare in Qoran the frequently 'And God is .. . . . [the mighty, the merciful, etc.]').

2 The ו‎ consecutive (formerly called the Waw 'conversive'); —

a. with the

imperfect (וַּ‎ with following daghesh; before וָ א,‎), as וַיּאֹמֶר‎ properly = and he proceeded to say, chiefly in contin. of a preceding perfect tense (so Moabite);

b. with the

perfect (וְ‎, — in 1 & 2 singular, the tone, with certain exceptions [see Dr§ 110], being thrown forward to the ultima), as וְיָָֽשַׁבְתָּ֫‎ properly so [namely, as limited by a verb, or other term, preceding] hadst thou sat, chiefly in continuation of a preceding imperfect tense, in its various senses of future, jussive, or frequentative. Thefurther analysis of these idioms belongs to the grammar; see on a DrCh. vi., Ges§ 111, and on

b DrCh. viii. Ges§ 112. Here it must suffice to note — (a) ו‎ consecutive (especially with the imperfect) frequently couples two verbs in such a manner that the first, indicating the general character of the action, receives its closer definition in the second: in such cases, the first may often be represented in English by an adverb, as Gen 26:18 וַיַּחְמֹּר וַיָּשָׁב‎ and he turned and dug = and he dug again; so often; and similarly with הוֺסִיף‎ 25:1, מִהַר‎ 24:18, הוֺאִיל‎ Josh 7:7, etc.; more exceptionally, Gen 30:27; Est 8:6, and (not consecutive) Gen 47:6; Job 23:3; Song 2:3; Lam 3:26 (see Ges§ 120, 2 a; compare in Syriac Nö§ 335-6. In Arabic the stronger form of the conjugation here corresponds: Wii. § 140). (b) וַּ ‎ with the imperfect sometimes expresses a contrast = and yet, Gen 32:31 I have seen God face to face וַתִּנָּצֵל‎ and yet my soul is delivered, Deut 4:33; 2Sam 3:8; 19:29; Isa 51:12; Psa 73:14; 144:3; Job 10:8 + (compare Dr§ 74 β). (c) there is a tendency in the later books of the OT to use the perfect with simple וְ‎, where the classical language would employ the imperfect with וַּ ‎ (compare above

1); so especially in Ecclesiastes, where וַּ ‎ occurs thrice only, Job 1:17; 4:1, 7. (d) a double perfect with ו‎ consecutive is sometimes used, informally but neatly, with a hypothetical force; thus (a) in past or present time Exod 16:21 וְנָמָֽס׃ הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ וְחַם‎ and the sun used to be warm, and it used to melt = and if (or when) the sun was warm, it melted, 33:10; 1Kin 18:10; Jer 18:4, 8 וְנִחַמְתִּ֫י וְֹשָׁב‎ = and if it turns, I repent, 20:9 (see RV); (β) in future time, Gen 44:22 ומת אביו ועזב‎ and he will leave his father, and he will die = and if he leaves his father, he will die, 33:13; 42:38; Exod 4:14; 12:13; 1Sam 16:2; 19:3; Ezek 33:3; 39:15 etc. (Dr§ 147-9, Ges§ 159. 2 e).

3 With a

voluntative (cohortative or jussive) וְ‎ expresses an intention, that or so that (an elegancy by which the too frequent use of לְמַעַן‎ or בַּעֲבוּר‎ is avoided): Exod 10:17 entreat God, וְיָסֵר‎ so may he remove (= that he may remove) this death, Gen 27:4 and bring it me וְאֹכֵ֑לָה‎ so let me eat (= that I may eat); and without the modal form being externally indicated, Exod 14:1 speak . . . וְיָשֻׁבוּ‎ that they return, 14:15; and often Sts. even of past time, as 1Kin 13:33 whom he would, he consecrated וִיהִי‎ that there might be priests of the high places, 2Kin 19:25; Isa 25:9 a Lam 1:19. After a negative, Psa 51:18 thou desirest not sacrifice, וְאֶתֵּ֑נָה‎ so [= in that case] would I give it (or, that I might give it), 55:13 וְאֶשָּׂא‎ so could I bear it (or, that I might bear it), Isa 53:2 RVm Num 23:19; Jer 5:28 RV. Sts. also before an imperative, Gen 12:2 and be (= that thou mayest be) a blessing, 2Sam 21:3 +. See more fully Dr§ 59-65, Ges§ 108. 2; 109. 2; 110. 2. (In Arabic with the subjunctive is used similarly: Wii. § 15 d.) A volunt. is also sometimes attached by וְ‎ to a preceding volunt. or imperative, so as to form a virtually hypothetical sentence, as Gen 42:18 וִחְיוּ עֲשׂוּ זֹאת‎ = if you do this, you shall live, 30:28; 34:12; Prov 3:9f. 4:4, 8; Isa 55:2: see Dr§ 152.

4 It expresses often an informal inference, or consequence, so, then, especially at the beginning of a speech: Gen 27:8; Psa 2:10 and often וְעַתָּה‎ now, therefore; וְלָמָּה‎ and וּמַדּוּעַ‎ why, then? Gen 29:25; Num 12:8; 16:3 +; Exod 2:20 וְאַיּוֺ‎ where, then, is he? Gen 34:21; 1Sam 15:14; 26:22 וְיַעֲבֹר‎ let, then, . . . come over, 2Sam 24:3; 2Kin 4:41 קֶמַח וּקְחוּ‎ then bring meal, Ezek 18:32. So the וְ‎ consecutive and the perfect, as Deut 2:4 וְנִשְׁמַרְתֶּם‎ take heed, therefore, 4:15; 7:9 וְיָָֽדַעְתָּ֫‎ know, therefore, 30:19; 1Sam 6:5; 1Kin 2:6; Ruth 3:9; Josh 15:19; Isa 40:6b (Dr§ 119 δ).

5 ו‎ introduces the predicate or apodosis: namely

a. וְ‎ consecutive and the Perfect — in answer to אִם‎ or כִּי‎ constantly, as Exod 19:5; 23:22 if thou hearkenest to my voice, וְאָֽיַבְתִּ֫י‎ then am I (= I will be) enemy to thy enemies (see Dr§ 136-8); after the casus pendens, 12:44 every servant that is bought for money, וּמַלְתָּ֫ה‎ thou shalt circumcise him, etc. Num 14:31; 24:24; 1Sam 25:27; 2Sam 14:10 he that spake unto thee, אֵלַי וַהֲבֵאתוֺ‎ so hast thou brought him (= thou shalt bring him) unto me, Isa 9:4; 56:6f. +; Exod 12:15; 31:14; Deut 17:12 +; after various time-determinations, as Gen 3:5 in the day of your eating from it וְנִפְקְחוּ‎ then shall your eyes be opened, Exod 16:6 וִידַעְתֶּם עֶרֶב‎ at even, then shall ye know, 16:7; 32:34; 2Sam 15:10; 1Kin 13:31 אֹתִי וּקְבַרְתֶּם בְּמוֺתִי‎ when I die, so ye shall bury me, etc., + often; after conjs., as כִּי‎ Gen 29:15, יַעַן‎ 1Kin 20:28; Isa 3:16f., תַּחַת‎ 60:15, etc., (see Dr§ 123).

b. וַּ ‎ consecutive and the imperfect (but much less frequently than the perfect), as Gen 30:30 the little that thou hadst, וַיִּפְרֹץ‎ it hath increased, Exod 9:21; 2Sam 4:10; 1Kin 9:20f. 15:13 +; after time-determinations, Gen 22:4 on the third day וַיִּשָּׂא‎ then Abraham lifted up his eyes, 19:15; 27:34; 37:18; 1Sam 6:6; 12:8; Isa 6:1; Hosea 11:1 when Israel was a child, וָאֹהֲבֵהוּ‎ then I loved him, +; occasionally after conjunctions, as כַּאֲשֶׁר‎ Exod 16:34, יַעַן‎ 1Sam 15:23, לְמַעַן‎ Isa 45:4, אִם‎ Psa 59:16 (Dr§ 127).

c. in other cases (not 'consecutive') — all more or less uncommon: namely a. וְ‎ closely joined to the imperfect Gen 13:9 if to the left, וְאֵימִינָה‎ then I will take the right (compare 2Sam 12:8) Exod 12:3 on the 10th of the month וְיִקְחוּ‎ then let them take, Num 16:5; Isa 43:4; Hosea 4:6; 10:10; Psa 69:33; Job 15:17; 2Sam 22:41; Prov 23:24 Kt (Dr§ 125); β. separated from the verb, Exod 8:22; Lev 7:16 יֵאָכֵל וְהַנּוֺתָר וּמִמָּחֳרָת‎ and on the morrow, then the remainder shall be eaten, Josh 3:3; 1Kin 8:32; Isa 8:7; 48:7; Job 14:7; 20:18; b 23:12; 25:5; 32:14 +; γ. without a verb, Gen 40:9 וְהִנֵּה בַּחֲלֹמִי‎ in my dream, behold, a vine was before me, 40:16; 2Sam 23:3f.; Prov 10:25, and the extreme cases 2Sam 15:34 thy father's slave, מֵאָז וַאֲנִי‎ I was that of old, — but now עַבְדְּךָ וַאֲנִי‎ well, I will be thine, Isa 34:12 (si vera lectio), Job 4:6b דְּרָכֶיךָ וְתֹם תִּקְוָָֽתְךָ‎ thy confidence — it is the uprightness of thy ways, 36:26 חֵקֶר וְלֹא שָׁנָיו מִסְמַּר‎ Ges. seine Jahre, da ist kein Zählen (compare Dr§ 124-5, 128-9). — With 4, 5 compare the Arabic , Wi. § 366 b, 367 c; ii. § 187; Dr§ 185 end.

Min, 1894): — 1. with verbs expressing (or implying) separation or removal, whether from a person or place, or in any direction, also from guilt, calamity, etc.: — thus

a. to descend from a mountain Exod 19:14, to fall from a roof Deut 22:8, from heaven Isa 14:12, to go up from a valley Josh 10:7, to raise up from the dunghill 1Sam 2:8, or the ground 2Sam 12:17. e. of the immediate, or efficient, cause (chiefly in poetry), in consequence of, at by (compare Greek ἀπό, as Hd. 2:54 ζήησιν ἀπὸ σφέων γενέσθαι): (a) the cause, a person Gen 19:36 + מן הָֽרְתָה‎ to be pregnant by, 49:25; 1Sam 31:3 מֵהַמּוֺרִים וַיָּחֶל‎ was in anguish from the archers, Hosea 7:4 מֵאֹפֶה בֹּעֵ֫רָה‎ (ni הֵם בֹּעֵר‎ leg.: see We), Psa 18:9; Nahum 1:5 ממנו רעשׁו הרים‎, Dan 11:31 (accents); with passive verb, Nahum 1:6 ממנו נִתְּצוּ הצורים‎, Psa 37:23 (compare Prov 20:24

d), Job 24:1; Eccl 12:11; Dan 8:11. (b) the cause, a thing, Gen 49:24 his arms were agile יעקב אביר מידי‎ from the hands, etc., Isa 6:4 the thresholds shook הַקּוֺרֵא מִקּוֺל‎ (so מקול‎ elsewhere, as 30:31; 33:3; Jer 8:16), 28:7 מִןהַֿשֵּׁכָר תָעוּ‎ (|| ב‎), 31:4, 9; 10:10; Ezek 19:10 became fruitful רַבִּים מִמַּיִם‎, 31:5; Job 4:9 יאֹבֵדוּ אֱלוֺהַּ מִנִּשְׁמַת‎ at the breath of God, 14:9 יַפְרִחַ מַיִם מֵרֵיחַ‎, 31:23; 39:26 יַאֲבֶרנֵֿץ הֲמִבִּינָָֽתְךָ‎ Psa 39:11; 73:19 מִןבַּֿלָּהוֺת תַּמּוּ סָפוּ‎, 78:65 מִיַּיִן מִתְרוֺנֵן‎, 104:15 משׁמן פנים להצהיל‎ from oil, 107:39, compare Job 7:14 (|| ב‎); so with י ׳מִגַּעֲרַת‎ at J.'s rebuke, 18:16; Job 76:7 +; with a passive verb, Gen 9:11 to be cut off הַמַּבּוּל מִמֵּי‎, 2Sam 7:29 יְבֹרַח וּמִכִּכָֽתְךָ‎, Isa 28:7 מןהֿיין נבלעו‎ are undone through wine (22:3 is dubious: see 1b), Obadiah 9; Job 28:4 רָ֑גֶל מִנִּי הַנִּשְׁכָּחִים‎; compare Isa 34:3; Hosea 6:8. (c) with verbs of fearing, to express the source of the emotion, as ירא‎ Psa 3:7 + often (also with מִמְּנֵי‎), מָּחַד‎ 27:1, נִבְהַל‎ Ezek 26:18, גּוּר‎ Deut 18:22; Job 41:17; Est 5:9 ממנו זָע ולא ולאקֿם‎; with בּוֺשׁ‎ to be disconcerted or disappointed, to express the source of the disappointment, Isa 1:29 + often; with שָׂמֵחַ‎ Prov 5:18; Eccl 2:10. feminine of the remoter cause, the ultimate ground on account of which something happens or is done. (N.B. The line between

e and

f. is not always clearly defined): Exod 2:23 they sighed מןהֿעבדה‎ on account of the bondage, 6:9; 15:23; Deut 7:7 not מֵרֻבְּכֶם‎ through, by reason of, your numbers did J. set his love upon you, Josh 22:24 to do a thing מִדְּאָנָה‎ out of carefulness, 2Sam 23:4 מִנֹּגַהּ‎, 1Kin 14:4; Isa 53:5 wounded מִמְּשָׁעֵינוּ‎ on account of our transgressions, bruised מֵעֲוֺנוֺתֵינוּ‎, 53:8; Job 4:19; Obadiah 10; Hab 2:17; Psa 6:8 מִכַּעַס עיני עשׁשׁה‎ from vexation (compare Job 17:7: Psa 31:10 ׳ב‎), 31:12; 38:19 I am concerned on account of my sin, Prov 20:4 יחרשׁ לא עצל מֵחֹרֶף‎ by reason of the winter, Job 22:4 יֹכִיחֶ֑ךָ הֲמִיִּרְאָ֑תְךָ‎ on account of thy fear of him? Song 3:8; Ruth 1:13 מִכֶּם מְאֹד כִּימַֿרלִֿי‎ because of you: see also Deut 28:34, 67; 32:19; Judg 2:18; Isa 65:14; Jer 12:4; 24:2 מֵרֹעַ‎, 50:13; 51:5 b (Ew Ke), Ezek 7:27 (but read probably with ᵑ9 ᵑ6 ᵐ5‎ Co כְּדרכם‎), 16:61; 35:11 (AV out of), 45:20; Micah 2:12; 7:13; Psa 5:11; 12:6; 107:17; 119:53; Gen 49:12 red of eyes מִיָּ֑יִן‎, and white of teeth מֵחָלָב‎. Often also in מֵרֹב‎ from the abundance of, absolute for abundance, with many different verbs, as 16:10 מֵרֹב יִסָּפֵר לֹא‎ Josh 9:13; 1Sam 1:16, etc. Similarly in מִבִּלְתִּי מִבְּלִי, מֵאֵין,‎ (pp. 35, 115, 117); and before an infinitive (7a), and in מֵאֲשֶׁר‎ (p. 84).

g. the cause being conceived as regulative, מן‎ occasionally approaches in sense to according to (compare Latin ex more, ex lege), Jonah 3:7 proclaimed in Nineveh וגדליו המלך מטעם‎ at, by, in accordance with, the decree of the king (compare Aramaic Ezra 6:14; Dan 2:8): so Job 39:26 (2e (b)) according to Ges Hi.

3 Partitively (a sense connecting with

2a (c), above): —

a. Gen 6:19 מִכֹּל שְׁנַיִם‎ two out of, from, all, 7:8; 39:11 ֗֗֗ מן אישׁ‎ a man (or one) of . . . (so Num 25:6; 1 Samuel 24:28 +, ֗֗֗ מן אנשׁים‎ 16:2; Josh 2:2 +, 2Kin 2:7, etc.); Gen 42:16 send אֶחָד מִכֶּם‎ Lev 1:2a 17:12 מִכֶּם כלנֿפשׁ‎, 19:34; 26:8, Judg 8:14 סֻכּוֺת מֵאַנְשֵׁי נַעַר‎, 1Sam 22:8, etc.; Judg 14:19; 2Kin 2:24; Isa 66:19; ֗֗֗ מִן אֶחָד‎ 1Sam 16:18 +, ֗֗֗ מִן אַחַד‎ (Ges§ 130, 1) Deut 25:5 +; מֵהֵ֫נָּה אַחַת‎ Psa 34:21; Isa 34:16; ֗֗֗ מִן מִי‎ Job 5:1; Isa 50:1, ֗֗֗ מִן אֵין‎ 1Sam 14:39; Isa 51:18; 21:11 מלילה מהֿ‎ how much of the night? 2Chr 31:3 מִןרְֿכוּשׁוֺ הַמֶּלָח וּמְנָת‎.

b. the number being omitted, מִן‎ is used indefinitely: — (a) = some of, — as subject Exod 16:27 מןהֿעם יצאו‎ there went out (some) of the people, Lev 25:49; 2Sam 11:17, 24, especially in late Hebrew Ezra 2:68, 70; 7:7; Neh 11:4, 25; 1Chr 4:42; 9:30, 32; 2Chr 17:11; 32:21; Dan 11:35; more frequently as object, especially with לקח‎, Gen 4:3 האדמה מִמְּרִי וַיָּבֵא‎ brought of the fruit of the ground, 30:14 give me בְנֵךְ מִדּוּדָאֵי‎ (some) of thy son's love-apples, 33:15; Exod 12:7; 17:5; Lev 18:30; 20:2; Num 11:17; 13:23; 1Kin 12:4; Isa 39:7; 47:13; Amos 2:11; Dan 8:10 +, Song 1:2 מִּיו מִנְּשִׁיקוֺת ישׁקני‎ let him kiss me (with) some of the kisses etc., Psa 72:15; 137:3 צִיּוֺן מִשִּׁיר‎ (some) of the songs of Zion, Job 11:6 (Ges RVm) + often; in late Hebrew note also ֗֗֗ מִן יֵשׁ‎ there are some of . . . Neh 5:5; ֗֗֗ מֵהֶם ֗֗֗ מֵהֶם‎ some. . . others. . . 1Chr 9:28f. (as in Aramaic Dan 2:33, and PS2155); ֗֗֗ מִקְצָת‎ some of. . . (as in Late Hebrew) 1:2; Neh 7:69. (b) to designate an individual (rare), Gen 28:11 and he took הַמָּקוֺם מֵאַבְנֵי‎ (one) of the stones of the place (see 28:18), Exod 6:25 פוטיאל מבּנות‎ (one) of the daughters of P., Ezek 17:5, 13; Neh 13:28; Psa 132:11; as subject Lev 25:33; Dan 11:5 the king of the south וּמִןֿ שָׂרָיו‎ and (one) of his captains, 11:7, compare Jer 41:1; Est 4:5; 2Chr 26:11; Ruth 2:20 הוא מִגֹּאֲלֵנוּ‎ he is (one) of our kinsmen, Exod 2:6. (c) in a negative or hypothetical sentence (whether subject or object) = any, aught, Deut 16:4 מןהֿבשׂר ילין ולא‎ and there shall not remain any of the flesh, 1Kin 18:5 מןהֿבהמה נכרית ולא‎ and we shall not destroy any of the beasts, 2Kin 10:10 (compare Josh 21:43; 23:14; 1Sam 3:19; 1Kin 8:56; Est 6:10), Esther 6:23 י מֵעַבְדֵי ׳מֶּןיֶֿשׁמֹּֿה‎ Job 27:6 מִיָּמָ֑י לְבָבִי יֶחֱרַף לֹא‎ my heart reproacheth not one of my days: with אִם‎, etc. Exod 29:34; Lev 4:2a (compare 4:22; 4:27), 11:32 (מהם‎), 11:33; 11:35; 11:37-39; 18:29; 25:25; Num 5:6; מִכֹּל‎ anything whatever, Leviticus 5:24; Lev 11:34; compare 1Sam 23:23 (?). (d) peculiarly, with a noun of unity, especially אֶחָד‎, to express forcibly the idea of a single one: Deut 15:7 if there be a poor man in thy midst, אַחֶיךָ מֵאַחַר‎ any one of thy brethren, Lev 4:2b if he doeth מֵהֵ֫נָּה מֵאַחַת‎ any one of these things, 5:13; Ezek 18:10 אָח וְעָשָׂה מֵאֵלֶּה מֵאַחַד‎ (where אח‎ is a vox nihili) and doeth aught of these things; 1Sam 14:45 if there shall fall אַרְצָה ראֹשׁוֺ מִשַּׂעֲרַת‎ a single hair of his head to the ground! (for שְׂעָרָה‎ as a noun of individual meaning see Ges§ 122t Dr), compare 2Sam 14:11; 1Kin 1:52. (Probably a rhetorical application of the partitive sense, though the explanation 'starting from one' = 'even one' would also be possible. is used similarly after negative and interrogative particles, not merely with collective nouns, as nought have they of knowledge (Qor 18:4), but also with nouns of unity, as Qor 3:55 Ye have not aught of (= any) god, except Him; 19:19 dost thou perceive even one of them? 6:59 there falleth not even a single leaf (noun of individual meaning) without His knowing it. See further Thes, and WAG. ii. § 48 f. b), (e) (rare) specifying the objects, or elements, of which a Genus consists (the Arabic , min of explication, WAG. ii. § 48 g): Gen 6:2 מכל בחרו אשׁר‎ consisting of all whom they chose, 7:22; 9:10; Lev 11:32 (מכל‎), 1Chr 5:18; Jer 40:7 (מאשׁר‎); 44:28 and they shall know וּמֵהֶם מִמֶּנִּי יָקוּם דְּבַרמִֿי‎ whose word shall stand, consisting of me and of them (defining the Genus embraced by ׃מי‎ compare both (of them), Abel as well as Cain, and Qor 3:193: Wl.c.). — On מֵאַיִן‎ 10:6-7, see אַיִן‎ near the end.

4 of time — namely

a. as marking the terminus a quo, the anterior limit of a continuous period, from, since Deut 9:24 אֶתְכֶם דַּעְתִּי מִיּוֺם‎ from the day of my (first) knowing you (so 1Sam 7:2; 8:8 + ); 18:9 וָהָֽלְאָה ההוא מהיום‎ from that day and onwards, simil. Lev 22:27; Num 15:23; Ezek 39:22; Isa 18:2, 7 (where מִןהֿוּא‎ = הוּא מֵאֲשֶׁר‎; compare Nahum 2:9 הִיא מִימֵי‎ = הִיא אֲשֶׁר מִימֵי‎); וָמָֽעְלָה ההוא מהיום‎ 1Sam 16:13; 30:25 (Hag 2:15, 18 apparently of time backwards); מֵאָז‎ from the time of . . . .; מִןהַֿבֶּטֶן‎ from the womb Judg 13:5, 7, אִמִּי מִבֶּטֶן‎ 16:17 +; ֗֗֗ מִימֵי‎ Hosea 10:9; Isa 23:7; Jer 36:2 +; מִיָּמֶיךָ‎ idiomatic = since thou wast born 1Sam 25:28; 1Kin 1:6 (מִיָּמָיו‎), Job 38:12; מִקֶּדֶם‎ from antiquity Hab 1:12; Psa 74:12; Isa 42:14 מֵעוֺלָם הֶחֱשֵׁיתִי‎ I have been silent since old time; מֵעַתָּה‎ from now, hence-forth Jer 3:4 +, מִיּוֺם‎ from to-day 43:13; Ezek 48:35, הזה מןהֿיום‎ Hag 2:19. See also 5c, 7 c. compare Exod 33:6 חוֺרֵב מֵהַר‎ from Horeb, Hosea 13:4 I am ׳י‎ thy God מִצְרַיִם מֵאֶרֶץ‎.

b. as marking the period immediately succeeding the limit, after: Gen 38:24 חֳדָשִׁים כְּמִשְׁלשׁ‎ after about three months it was told Judah, רַבִּים מִיָּמִים‎ Josh 23:1; Ezek 38:8, מִיָּמִים‎ after (some) days, Judg 11:4; 14:8; 15:1, מִיֹּמַיִם‎ after two days Hosea 6:2; יָמִים מֵרֹב‎ Isa 24:22: more frequently with קֵץ‎ or קָצֶה‎, Gen 4:3 יָמִים מִקֵּץ‎, 8:3; Josh 3:2 + often; Deut 14:28 שָׁנִים שָׁלשׁ מִקְצֵה‎, 15:1 שֶׁבַע מִקְצֵה שָׁנִים‎ (by which is meant not the actual end of the three or seven years, but the period when the third or seventh year has arrived); מִמָּחֳרָת‎ after the morrow (had arrived) = on the morrow, Gen 19:34 + often; מֵהַבֹּקֶר‎ 2Sam 2:27. — 23:4 מִמָּטָר‎; Isa 53:11 נַפְשׁוֺ מֵעֲמַל‎; perhaps 29:18 (Kö581). compare 2Sam 20:5 and he delayed מןהֿמועד‎ beyond the appointed time.

c. in such phrases, however, מִן‎ sometimes (compare 1c) loses its significance: thus מֵאָז‎ 2Sam 15:34; Isa 16:13 not from former time, but in former time, formerly, Gen 6:4 מֵעוֺלָם אֲשֶׁר הַגִּבּוֺרִים‎ which were of old, Josh 24:2 dwelt of old, Psa 77:6 days מִקֶּדֶם‎ aforetime, מֵאַחֲרֵי‎ Deut 29:21 (p. 30). — מִקָּרוֺב‎ literally from near, i.e. recently 32:17, of short duration Job 20:5, shortly Ezek 7:8; at hand (in a local sense, 1c) Jer 23:23.

5 (וְעַד‎) עַד ֗֗֗ מִן‎ from . . . even, to : very oft .: —

a. in geography or local sense, Gen 10:19; 15:18 הגדול הנהר עד מצרים מנהר‎, 25:18; Exod 23:31; Deut 2:36; 1Sam 3:20; 2Sam 5:25; Jer 31:38; Psa 72:8 + often; so with מִלְּבוֺא‎ 1Kin 8:65 (2Chr 7:8), 2Kin 14:25; Amos 6:14; Deut 13:8 הָאָרֶץ קְצֵה וְעַד הָאָרֶץ מִקְצֵה‎, 28:64; Jer 12:12; Gen 47:21 וְעַדקָֿצֵהוּ גְּבוּלמִֿצְרַיִם מִקְצֵה‎, 1Kin 6:24; 7:23 וְעַד מִשְּׂפָתוֺ שְׂפָתוֺ‎; Lev 13:12 רגליו ועד מראשׁו‎, Deut 28:35 רגלך מכף קדקדך ועד‎ (similarly 2Sam 14:25; Job 2:7; Isa 1:6). compare 1Sam 9:2 וָמַ֫עְלָה מִשִּׁכְמוֺ‎, 2Sam 5:9; Josh 15:46.

b. metaphor not of actual space, but of classes of objects, to express idiomatically the idea ofcomprehension, so that the two prepositions may be often represented by both . . . and: Gen 19:4 וְעַדזָֿקֵן מִנַּעַר‎ from young to old (i.e. both included) = both young and old, 19:11; 1Sam 5:9 + וְעַדגָּֿדוֺל מִקָּטֹן‎ = both great and small, Jer 6:13 וְעַדגְּֿדוֺלָם מִקְּטַנָּם‎ from the least of them even to the greatest of them, ib. מִנָּבִיא וְעַדכֹּֿהֵן‎ from the prophet even to the priest every one dealeth falsely, Exod 9:25 + בהמה ועד מאדם‎ both man and beast, 11:5 וגו השׁפחה ׳בכור פרעהע֗֗֗ד מבכור‎, 13:15; Num 6:4; Deut 29:10 עציך מחֹטב מימיך שֹׁאב עד‎, Josh 8:25 + אשׁה ועד מאישׁ‎, 1Sam 15:3 (4 pairs), 22:19; 1Kin 5:13; 2Kin 17:9 = 18:8, Isa 10:18 בשׂר ועד מנפשׁ‎ = both soul and body, Jer 9:9; after a word implying a negative = either . . . or Gen 14:23; 31:24, 29 רע עד מטוב‎ either good or evil. The עַד‎ may be repeated, if required: 6:7 מאדם השׁמים ועדעֿוף רמשׂ עד עדבֿהמה‎ (so 7:23), Exod 22:3; Josh 6:21; Judg 15:5 זָ֑יִת וְעַדכֶּֿרֶם וְעַדקָֿמָה מִגָּדִישׁ‎, 20:48; 1Sam 30:19: without מן‎, Lev 11:42; Num 8:4. Similar is the use of מן‎ in the idiom (וָמָֽטָּה‎) וָמָֽעְלָה מִבֶּןשָׁ֗֗֗נָה‎ (also שָׁנָה ֗֗֗ וְעַדבֶּֿן‎); and compare 2Kin 3:21

c. of time, Gen 46:34 עַתָּה וְעַד מִנְּעֻרֵינוּ‎ from our youth even until now, 1Sam 12:2; Jer 3:25; Num 14:19; Exod 10:6; 18:13 עדהֿערב מןהֿבֹקר‎, 1Sam 30:17; 1Kin 18:26; Isa 9:6; Psa 90:2; + often: with two inff. Hosea 7:4: and implying intervals (not duration) Ezek 4:10-11, (compare with לְ‎ Est 3:7 (twice in verse)).

d. there occur further (1) אֶלֿ ֗֗֗ מִן‎, Josh 15:21; Exod 26:28 = 36:33 אֶלהַֿקָּצֶה מִןהַֿקָּצֶה‎ from end to end, Ezek 40:23, 27; Ezra 9:11 מִמֶּהאֶֿלמֶּֿה‎; Psa 144:13 זַן אֶל מִזַּן‎ from kind to kind = kinds of every sort; with a verb of motion, Jer 48:11; Psa 105:13; 1Chr 17:5, and expressing a climax, Psa 84:8 אֶלחַֿיִל מֵחַיִל יֵָֽלְכוּ‎, Jer 9:2 (compare Rom 1:17): of time, מיוםאֿליֿום‎ Num 30:15, compare 1Chr 16:23 (|| Psa 96:2 לְ‎); implying intervals, אֶלעֵֿת מֵעֵת‎ 1Chr 9:25. (2) לְ ֗֗֗ מִן‎ Exod 32:27; Ezek 40:13; Zech 14:10: of time Psa 96:2; Job 4:20: with intervals, 2Sam 14:26. (3) הָ֯ ֗֗֗ מִן‎ Num 34:10; Ezek 6:14; רִבְלָ֫תָה מִמִּדְבָּר‎ (so Ges Ew Hi etc.) from the wilderness to Riblah, 21:3; 25:13 וּדְדָ֫נֶה מִתֵּימָן‎ (Co Kö Berthol); without ָ֯‎ 1Kin 5:1. And of time in the phrase (implying intervals) יָמִ֫ימָה מִיָּמִים‎ Exod 13:10 4t.

6 In comparisons, beyond, above, hence in English than: so constantly: namely

a. when an object is compared with another distinct from itself, Judg 14:18 מִדְּבַשׁ מַהמָּֿתוֺק‎ what is sweet away from, beyond in excess of, honey ? i.e. in our idiom, what is sweeter than honey ? Lev 21:10 מֵאֶחָיו הַגָּדוֺל הַכֹּהֵן‎ the priest that is great above his brethren, Num 14:12; Ezek 28:3 מִדָּנִאֵל חָכָם‎ wiser than Daniel, Psa 119:72 + very often; Hosea 2:9 מֵעָ֑תָּה אָז לִי טוֺב כִּי‎; with an infinitive (sometimes with לְ‎) as subject, Gen 29:10 וגו אֹתָהּ מִתִּתִּי לְךָ אֹתָהּ תִּתִּי ׳טוֺב‎ better is my giving her to thee than my giving her to another, Exod 14:12; 1Sam 15:22; Prov 21:9, 19; 25:7; Psa 118:8; 118:9 +; with verbs, Gen 19:9 מֵהֶם לְךָ נָרַע עתה‎ now we will harm thee beyond them, more than them, 25:23 יֶאֱמַץ מִלְאֹם לְאֹם‎, 26:16; 29:30 גםֿ ויאהב מִלֵּאָה אתרֿחל‎, 38:26 מִמֶּנִּי צָֽדְקָה‎, 48:19 מִמֶּנּוּ יִגְדַּל‎, Judg 2:19 מאבותם השׁחיתו‎ they have done corruptly more than their fathers, 1Sam 2:29; 2Sam 20:6; 1Kin 1:37; 14:9; Jer 5:3; Ezek 5:6 + often; = in, preference to, above, Psa 45:8; 52:5 (twice in verse); Hosea 6:6; Hab 2:16, after בחר‎ Jer 8:3; Job 7:15; 36:21; Psa 84:11 (מִדּוּר‎) +: note also מִן נֹפֵל‎ Job 12:3; 13:2 +?to (Ew Ges and others Hi; al. De); מִן שֹׁנֶה‎ different from Est 1:7; 3:8.

b. when an object is compared with a group or multitude of which it forms one, especially with מִכֹּל‎, Gen 3:1 עָרוּם הַשָּׂדֶה חַיַּת מִכֹּל‎ subtil out of all beasts of the field, or beyond, above all (other) beasts, 3:14 cursed above all cattle (but without implying any judgment whether other cattle are cursed likewise), 37:3 Israel loved Joseph מִכָּלבָּֿנָיו‎ out of all his sons, or above all his (other) sons, Deut 7:7; 33:24 אָשֵׁר מִבָּנִים בָּרוּךְ‎ blessed above sons be Asher, Judg 5:24 מִנָּשִׁים תְּבֹרַח‎ blessed above women be Jael, 1Sam 9:2b 15:33 אִמֶּ֑ךָ מִנָּשִׁים תִּשְׁכַּל כֵּן‎, 18:30; Jer 17:9 מִכֹּל עָקֹב‎ deceitful above all things, Psa 45:3; Song 5:10 מֵרְבָבָה דָּגוּל‎ (compare מִן בָּחַר‎ above

2a c: ex in eximius, egregius; Iliad 18:431 ὅς σ’, ἐμοὶ ἐκ πάσεων Κρονίδης Ζεὺς ἄλγἐ ἔδωκεν, 3:227 ἔξοχος Ἀργείων . . . κεφαλήν).

c. sometimes in poetry the idea on which מן‎ is logically dependent, is unexpressed, and must be understood by the reader, Isa 10:10 מירושׁלם ופסיליהם‎ and their idols are (more) than (those of) Jerusalem, Micah 7:4 מִמְּסוּכָה יָשָׁר‎ the uprightest is (sharper) than a thorn-hedge (but We from), Job 11:7; 28:18; Psa 4:8 מֵעֵת‎ beyond (that of) the time when etc. Ecclesiastes 4:17; Eccl 9:17; compare Ezek 15:2.

d. מן‎ not unfrequently expresses the idea of a thing being too much for a person, or surpassing his powers: Gen 18:14 ׳מי הֲיִמָּלֵא דָּבָר‎ can a thing be too hard for J.? (so Deut 17:8 +; compare Psa 131:1; 139:6 + ), 32:11 מִן קָטֹנְתִּי‎, Deut 14:24 הַדֶּרֶךְ מִמְּךָ יִרְבֶּה כִּי‎ = is too great for thee (1Kin 19:7), 1Ki 32:47 מִכֶּם רֵק‎: so with עָצַם‎ Gen 26:16, כָּבֵד‎ be too heavy for Exod 18:18; Psa 38:5, מָךְ‎ Lev 27:8 (too poor to pay), קָשָׁה‎ Deut 1:7, צַר‎ be too narrow for, 2Kin 6:1; Isa 49:19, קצר‎ 50:2, אָמַץ‎ Psa 18:18, נמני ירום‎ is too high for me 61:3, גָּבַר‎ 65:4; מִמְּךָ ַהמְעַט‎ Job 15:11 too little for thee ? מִכֶּם ַהמְעַט‎ Num 16:9; Isa 7:13; Ezek 34:18 (see מְעַט‎; also on 16:20); often with an infinitive, as Gen 4:13 מִנְּשׂוֺא עֲוֺנִי גָּדוֺל‎ is greater than I can bear, 30:7 their substance was יַחְדָּו מִשֶּׁבֶת רַב‎ literally great beyond dwelling together = too great for (their) dwelling together, Exod 12:4; Judg 7:2 רַב מִתִּתִּי‎ = too great for me to give, 1Sam 25:17b 1Kin 8:64 מֵהָכִיל רַב‎, Isa 28:20; 33:19; 59:1; Hab 1:13; Psa 40:6; Ruth 1:12: note especially מִן רַב‎ it is more than that . . . (= there is enough of), Exod 9:28; 1Kin 12:28, followed by substantive Ezek 44:6 (see רַב‎); and Isa 49:6 וגו לְהָקִים ׳עֶבֶד לִי מִהְיוֺתְךָ נָקֵל‎ too light for thy being my servant was it to raise up, etc., Ezek 8:17 וגו ׳מֵעֲשׂוֺת יִשְׂר לְבֵית ׳הֲנָקֵל‎ was it too trifling to the house of Israel for the doing etc. (less than the doing etc. deserved) ? (but ? read עֲשׂוֺת‎ on analogue of 1Kin 16:31).

7 מן‎ is prefixed to an infin.:

a. with a causal force (rare), from, on account of, through (compare 2f): Deut 7:7-8, י ׳מֵאַהֲבַת אֶתְכֶם‎ through J.'s loving you = because J. loved you, 9:28 (compare 1:27 בְּ‎) 2Sam 3:11 אֹתוֺ מִיִּרְאָתוֺ‎ = because he feared him, Isa 48:4 ֗֗֗ מִדַּעְתִּי‎ = because I knew. . . So in מִבִּלְתִּי , ֗֗֗ מִבְּלִי‎.

b. after verbs implying restraint, prevention, cessation, etc., as עֲצָרַנִי מִלֶּדֶת‎ Gen 16:2 hath restrained me from bearing, מִלֶּדֶת וַתַּעֲמֹד‎ 29:35; 30:9: so with חשׂך‎ 20:6 +, חדל‎ + Exod 23:5 +, כִּלָּה‎ + 34:33 +, נִכְלָא‎ 36:6, מָנַע‎ 1Sam 25:26 +, שׁבת‎ Jer 31:36 +, מֵהַבִּיט יָרֵא‎ Exod 3:6 +, מִןהַֿחֵרֶם שִׁמְרוּ‎ Josh 6:18; 2Chr 25:13 מִלֶּכֶת הֵשִׁיב‎. Especially (a) after similar verbs, expressing concisely a negative consequence, literally away from . . ., i.e. so as not to, so that not: Gen 23:6; b 27:1 Jacob's eyes were dim, ֵמרְאֹת‎ away from seeing = so that he could not see, 31:29 מִן נִשְׁמַר‎ (|| 31:24 מֶּן‎), Exod 14:5; Lev 26:13; Num 32:7; Deut 28:55 (his eye shall be envious etc.) מִתֵּת‎ from giving = so that he will not give, Judg 6:27; 1 Samuel 21:31; 1Sam 7:8 do not be silent from us מִזְּעֹק‎ so as not to call (compare 1Kin 22:3), 1Sam 8:7 me have they rejected עליהם מִמְּלֹךְ‎, 16:1 (Hosea 4:6), 2Sam 14:11 (read מֵהַרְבּוֺת‎), Isa 5:6; 8:11; 21:3; 23:1 is destroyed מִבּוֺא‎ so that none can enter in, 24:10; 33:15; 44:18; 49:15; 54:9; 56:6; 58:13; Jer 10:14 מִדַּעַת ֗֗֗ נִבְעַר‎ is stupefied so that he has no knowledge, 13:14; 33:21, 24, 26; Ezek 20:17; Micah 3:6; Zech 7:11; 7:12; Psa 30:4 Qr, 39:2; 69:24; 102:5 (after שָׁכַח‎, peculiarly), 106:23; Lam 3:44; 4:18; Job 34:30a 2Chr 36:13. So in מֵעֲשׂוֺת חָלִילָהלִֿי‎ that I should not do Gen 44:17 +. (b) still more concisely, especially in poetry, with a noun alone: 1Sam 15:23 has rejected thee מִמֶּלֶךְ‎ from (being) king (15:26 מִהְיוֺת מֶלֶךְ‎), Lev 26:43 מֵהֶם‎, Isa 7:8 מֵעָם יֵחַת‎ shall be shattered from (being) a people, that it be no more a people, 17:1 מֵעִיר מוּסָר‎, 25:2b; 52:14 מִשְׁחַת כֵּן מַרְאֵהוּ מֵאִישׁ‎ marred away from (being) a man('s), Jer 2:25 מִיָּחֵף‎, 17:16 מֵרֹעֶה‎, 48:2 מִגּוֺי וְנַכְרִיתֶנָּה‎, 48:42 מֵעָם‎, Psa 8:6 hast made him lack but little מאלהים‎ ut non esset Deus, 83:5 מִגּוֺי‎, Prov 30:2 בַּעַר מֵאִישׁ אָנֹכִי‎ too boorish to be a man: compare Dan 4:13; 1Kin 15:13 מִגְּבִירָה וַיְסִרֶהָ‎ removed her from (being) queen-mother, Ezek 16:41 מִזּוֺנָה וִהִשְׁבַּתִּיךְ‎; and even to express absolutely the non-existence of a thing not named in the principal clause, as Isa 23:1 כִּי מִבַּיִת שֻׁדַּד‎ so that there is no house, Ezek 12:19 (32:15), 25:9 מֵהֶעָרִים‎, Hosea 9:11 (3 t. in verse); 9:12; Micah 3:6; Hag 1:10 מִטָּ֑ל‎, Zech 7:14; 9:8; Psa 39:3; 49:15 מִזְּבֻללֿוֺ‎ so that it has no dwelling, 52:7 מֵאֹהֶל יִסָּֽחֲךָ‎ pluck thee up tentless, 109:24 is lean מִשָּׁ֑מֶן‎ so that there is no fatness, Job 28:11; 33:21; 34:30b. Oft. strengthened by pleonastic אֵין‎ or בְּלִי‎, as יוֺשֵׁב מֵאֵין‎ Isa 5:9, יוֺשֵׁב מִבְּלִי‎ see pp. 35:a, 115:b. compare Köiii. 592 ff.

c. with a temporal force, since, after (compare

4), chiefly late: Num 24:23 אֵל מִשֻּׂמוֺ‎ after God's establishing him, Isa 44:7 עֿוֺלָם עַם מִשֻּׂמִי‎ since I appointed the ancient people, Hosea 7:4; Hag 2:16 (?) Ruth 2:18; Neh 5:14; 1Chr 8:8 אוֺתָם מִןשִֿׁלְחוֺ‎ (compare 6:16) 2Chr 31:10; Dan 11:23; 12:1 (compare 9:25), Psa 73:20 מֵהָקִיץ כַּחֲלוֺם‎ after (one's) awaking, Job 20:4.

8 Once Deut 33:11 as a

conjunction before a finite verb. Smite . . . his haters מִןיְֿקוּמוּן‎ that they rise not again, in poetry for מִקּוּם‎ (7b): compare Dr§ 41. — On מֵאֲשֵׁר‎

adverb and

conjunction.

9 In compounds: —

a. מִלְּ מִבַּ֫עַד, מִבַּלְעֲדֵי, מִבֵּין, מֵאֵת, מֵאַחֲרֵי,‎ (common in Late Hebrew, **for מִלְּ‎ in Mishna see e.g. Babylonian Mez 7:10; Kil 8:1; Ter 8:11; Pes 1:6; Taan 2:7; Yeb 8:2; Ecclesiastes 4:17 מִלַּעֲשׂוֺת‎ (have no knowledge so as not to do evil) is read by Siegf Wild; especially before infinitive; in O.T. only in מִלְּבוֺא מִלְּבַד,‎ (above 5a), מִלִּפְנֵי מִלְּפָנִים, מִלְּעֻמַּת, מִלְמַ֫טָּה, מִלְמַ֫עְלָה,‎, and, si vera lectio, הֶחָ֑רֶס מִלְמַעֲלֵה‎ Judg 8:13, see מַעֲלֶה‎), מִתַּ֫חַת מֵעִם, מֵעַל, מִנֶּגֶד,‎; see אֵת אַחֲרֵי,‎, etc.

b. לְמִן‎ (לְמִנִּי‎ Micah 7:12 (twice in verse)), with לְ‎ pleonastic, from = מִן‎, but used almost exclusively of the terminus a quo, whether of space or time (compare מִן‎

5); — (I) of space, Deut 4:32; Judg 20:1 שֶׁבַע וְעַדבְּֿאֵר לְמִדַּן‎, Micah 7:12.7:12 (both לְמִנִּי‎), Zech 14:10; 1Chr 5:9; לְמֵרָחוֺק‎ from afar Job 36:3; 39:29 (on Ezra 3:13; 2Chr 26:15, see below לְ עַד‎); לְ לְמִתַּחַת‎ = underneath 1Kin 7:32. Idiomatic, especially followed by וְעַד‎, to denote comprehensively an entire class, בְּהֵמָה וְעַד לְמֵאִישׁ‎ Exod 11:7; Jer 51:62 (לְמֵאָדָם‎), אִשָּׁה וְעַד לְמֵאִישׁ‎ 2Sam 6:19; 2Chr 15:13, גָּדוֺל וְעַד לְמִקָּטֹן‎ 2Kin 23:2; Jer 42:8, simil. 2Chr 15:13; Jer 31:34; Est 1:5, 20, וְעַדטֿוֺב לְמֵרָע‎ 2Sam 13:22, שָׁנָה עֶשְׂרִים לְמִבֶּן וּלְמָ֑טָּה‎ 1Chr 27:23, compare 2Chr 25:5. — On לְמִבֵּית‎ Num 18:7. (2) of time (often following by עַד‎), ֗֗֗ אֲשֶׁר הַיּוֺם לְמִן‎ from the day when . . ., Deut 4:32; 9:7; 2Sam 7:11 (|| 1Chr 17:10 אֲשֶׁר וּלְמִיָּמִים‎) Jer 7:25; 32:31; Hag 2:18; ֗֗֗ אֲשֶׁר הַיָּמִים לְמִקְצָת‎ Dan 1:18; הַיּוֺם לְמִן‎ followed by infinitive (in apposition) Exod 9:18; 2Sam 19:25; לְמִיּוֺם‎ followed by infinitive (genitive) Judg 19:30; 2Sam 7:6; Isa 7:17; ֗֗֗ לְמִימֵי‎ 2Kin 19:25 (|| Isa 37:26 מימי‎) Mal 3:7; למןֿ עולם ועד עולם‎ Jer 7:7; 25:5; לְמֵרָחוֺק‎ from afar = long before, 2Sam 7:19 = 1Chr 17:17; 2Kin 19:25 = Isa 37:26.

מְנָאוֺת‎ see מְנָת‎ below מנה‎. below

[מַנְגִּינָה‎] see נגן‎.

II. מִנֵּי מִנִּי,‎ see מִן‎. מִנִּי‎ Psa 45:9 see I. [ מֵן‎].

מִנָיוֺת‎ see מְנָת‎ below מנה‎.

מִנְיָמִן מִנְיָמִין,‎ see מִיָּמִן‎.

מִנְלָם‎ see [ מִנְלֶה‎] below נלה‎.

מנן‎ (of following; Arabic is praecidit funem, diminuit numerum,debilitavit; also be bounteous, Qor 3:158 and elsewhere, a gift; whence ZerweckPräp. Min 4 assumes a primary meaning to separate — either from or for ("zutheilen"), as the case might be).

דגן.def:
H1715. dagan

דָּגָן‎ noun masculine corn, grain (of cereals) (Late Hebrew id., Samaritan see Thes.; compare Phoenician דגן ארצת‎) — דָּגָן‎ Gen 27:28-29t.; construct דְּגַן‎ Psa 78:24; suffix דְּגָנִי‎ Hosea 2:11, דְּגָָֽנְךָ‎ Deut 7:13; 12:17; 14:23; 18:4, דְּגָנֶ֑ךָ‎ 11:14, דְּגָנֵךְ‎ Isa 62:8, דְּגָנָם‎ Psa 4:8; 65:10 — corn, with תִּירוֺשׁ‎ must, q. v., Gen 27:28, 37 (both J) Psa 4:8; Isa 62:8; Hosea 2:11; 7:14; 9:1; Zech 9:17; compare also Num 18:27 (P; here, for מִןהַֿיָּ֑קֶב מְלֵאָה תירושׁ,‎), Lam 2:12 (where יַיִן‎), Hosea 14:8 (where גֶּפֶן‎ & יֵין לְבָנוֺן‎); ותירושׁ דגן ארץ‎ of land of Canaan Deut 33:28; of land of captives (words of the Rabshak) 2Kin 18:32 = Isa 36:17 (other products, also, named in both); usually with תירושׁ‎ & יצהר‎ Num 18:12; Deut 7:13; 11:14; 12:17; 14:23; 18:4; 28:51; 2Chr 31:5 (+דבשׁ‎) 32:28; Neh 5:11; Nehemiah 10:40; 13:5, 12; Jer 31:12; Hosea 2:10; Hosea 2:24; Joel 1:10; 2:19; Hag 1:11; also Joel 1:17 Me; (compare 2Kin 18:32; Isa 36:17 above); alone, rare and late Neh 5:2-3, 10; Psa 65:10; Ezek 36:29; דְּגַןשָֿׁמַיִם‎ Psa 78:24; — of the above the following refer to firstfruits offered to the priests Num 18:12 (compare 18:27) Deut 18:4; 2Chr 31:5; to tithe Deut 12:17; 14:23; Neh 13:5, 12; to both Generally Nehemiah 10:40; to loaning on usury 5:10-11,.

דגר.def:
H1716. dagar

[דָּגַר‎] verb gather together as a brood (compare Aramaic דְּגַר‎ heap together; so Nasar.) —

Qal Perfect3masculine singular דָּ֨גָר‎ Jer 17:11; 3feminine singular דָּֽגְרָה‎ Isa 34:15 — gather together into its shadow 34:15 (of קִמֹּז‎, q. v.), יָלָד֑ וְלֹא דָּגָר‎ Jer 17:11 (of partridge; simile of one getting riches unjustly).

דד.def:
H1717. dad

[דַּד‎] noun masculineProv 5:19 breast, better teat, nipple (τιτθοί Aq 5:19 Symm Ezek 23:3, 21; Late Hebrew & Aramaic דַּד‎; primitive caressing word; according to Fl in NHWBi. 489) — Du. construct דַּדֵּי‎ 23:3, 8) both strike out ᵑ6 ᵐ5‎ Co); suffix דַּדַּיִךְ‎ 23:21 (read ᵑ6 בתוליך‎ Co); דַּדֶּיהָ‎ Prov 5:19; — of breasts of woman 5:19; (Hi Bi read דֹּדֶיהָ‎ her love compare 7:18); of Samaria & Jerusalem under figure of young women Ezek 23:3 (בְּתוּלֵיהֶן דַּדֵּי‎) compare 23:8; דַּדַּיִךְ‎ 23:21; but probably strike out ׳ד‎ in Ezekiel compare above & GeiUrachrift 397. — See also שַׁד‎ below שׁדה‎.

דֹּדָה דֹּד,‎ see below דוד‎.

דדה.def:
H1718. dadah

[דָּדָה‎] verb [move slowly] (Late Hebrew Pi`el דִּדָּה‎ lead slowly, Hithpa`el הִדַּדָּה‎; Aramaic אִידַּדִּי דַּדִּי,‎; Arabic is run quickly (of a camel): on form, compare Köi. 587; SS derive from דאה‎ compare Sta§ 112 a, 150 a. 129 b, 581 d) —

Pi`el Imperfect1singular suffix אֲדַדֵּם‎ (so read for אֶדַּדֵּם ᵑ0‎ Dy Bi & Che, compare his critical note) lead slowly (in procession) Psa 42:5.

Hithpa`el Imperfect1singular אֶדַּדֶּה‎ Isa 38:15; also suffix אֶדַּדֵּם‎ Psa 42:5 ᵑ0‎ but compare above; — walk deliberately, at ease (De Che Di), or as in procession (Ew), Isa 38:15 (compare Che Di VB).

דדוהו.def:
H1735. Dodavahu

דדן.def:
H1719. Dedan

or Dedaneh דְּדָן‎ proper name, of a location & a people; — ׳ד‎ Gen 10:7-8t. + Ezek 27:20 (but see below) with ה‎ locative דְּדָ֫נֶה‎ 25:13 compare Ges§ 90, 2 near the end; —

1 under figure of son of רַעֲמָה‎ and grandson of כּוּשׁ‎ (see these arts.) Gen 10:7 (brother of שְׁבָא‎) = 1Chr 1:9; Ezek 27:20; compare ד ׳בְּנֵי‎ 27:15 (but read here perhaps ᵐ5 רדן‎ υιὁὶ Ῥοδίων, compare StaDe Pop. Javan. 11, also ᵑ6‎ Co; see below דֹּדָנִים‎ below) compare also 38:13, וּד ׳שְׁבָא‎; south-Arabian tribe on Persian Gulf, = Sabean דדן בנו‎ according to DHMZMG 1876, 122; Sab. Denkm. 28 (dubit. Mordt); but in northwest of Arabian peninsula, GlaserSkizze ii. 391 ff.; perhaps originally further south compare Di Gen 10:7.

2 as son of יָקְשָׁן‎ father of אַשּׁוּרִם‎ etc., Gen 25:3 (twice in verse) (here also brother of שְׁבָא‎) = 1Chr 1:32; Jer 25:23; 49:8 ד ׳ישְׁבֵי‎. This is apparently a northern branch of 1, compare Di Gen 25:3. — On דדן‎ in MI31, 31 compare Sm & SoMI p. 29 NöLCB Jan. 8, 1887 ClGannJAssyrian Jan. 1887. 107.

דְּדָ֫נֶה‎ see דְּדָןָ‎.

רֹדָן‎ proper name, of a location or a people Rhodes, Rhodians, so read, ר ׳בְּנֵי‎ Ezek 27:15 (for דְּדָן בְּנֵי ᵑ0‎, see ׳ד‎ 1), ᵐ5‎ Sta Co Berthol Toy Krae.

דדני.def:
H1720. Dedani

[דְּדָנִי‎] adjective, of a people only plural as substantive דְּדָנִים אֹרְחוֺת‎ Isa 21:3.

דהב.def:
H1722. dehab

דָּהָב‎23 noun masculineDan 2:32 gold (so ᵑ7‎ Syriac; Biblical Hebrew זָהָב‎); — absolute ׳ד‎ 2:32 +, דְּהַ֑ב‎ Ezra 7:15; emphatic דַּהֲבָה‎ 5:14; 6:5; 7:18, בָא‎- Dan 2:35 15t. Daniel.

דהי.def:
H1768. di

דִּי‎ particle of relation, who, which, that, used also as

mark of Genitive and

conjunction that, because (Aramaic of Nineveh, Babylonian, Zinjirli, Nerab, Cilicia, Têma, Egypt, ןי‎ (Lzb267. 446 RES361 S-CPap. A 2 +); Nabataean, Palmyrene די‎; דְּ ᵑ7‎ (except in compounds, as דִּילִי‎ mine, דִּילֵיהּ‎ his); Samaritan ; Syriac ; Ethiopic za: of same origin as Arabic possessor of [compare below Biblical Hebrew זֶה‎]. Properly a demonstrative that [compare זֶה‎; in Ethiopic ze is 'this', za 'which']; but this being referred by usage to something preceding becomes equivalent to the relative who, which, used, however, more widely than Hebrew אֲשֶׁר‎); — 1 as rel. who, which (construed like אֲשֶׁר‎): a. Jer 10:11; Dan 2:11 מְדָֽרְהוֺן דִּי‎ whose dwelling, 2:24 מַלְבָּא מַנִּי דִּי‎ whom the king had appointed, 2:26 בּ שְׁמֵהּ ׳דִּי‎ whose name was B., 4:5; 5:12, 23, etc.; = that which 2:23; = him that Ezra 7:25; 6:15; Dan 7:17 אַרְבַּע אִנוּן דִּת‎ which are four (see אִנּוּן‎). Following pronoun of 2 person (compare אֲשֶׁר‎ 3), 2:37 thou, O king ..., לָח יְהַב ֗֗֗ דִּי‎ to whom... hath given, 4:19; 4:6 as to whom I know, etc. (compare אֲשֶׁר‎ 4d end). Sq. תַּמָּה‎ = where Ezra 6:1, so דִּי‎ alone 6:3; Dan 2:38; of time, דִּי בְּעִדָּנָא‎ at the time when, etc., 3:5, 15. With the predicate an infinitive with לְ‎, 6:9 לְהַשְׁנָיָה לָא דִּי כְּתָבָא‎ which is not to be changed, Ezra 6:8; a place- or other determination, Dan 3:20 valiant men בְחֵילֵהּ‎ that were in his army, 5:2 בִירוּשְׁלֵב דִּי הֵיכְלָא‎, 7:20; Ezra 4:24; 5:6; 6:2, 6; compare Dan 2:25; 5:13; 7:7; Ezra 7:23. לָא דִּי‎ = without, 6:9; 7:22 (so ᵑ7 דְּלָא‎ Gen 15:2; Exod 21:11); compare Dan 2:34, 45. b. דִּי מָה דִּי, מָן‎ (compare in late Hebrew מַה ׳מַהשֶּֿׁ,‎ 1e b) whoever, whatever, so 3:6, 11 ָ(מןדִּֿילָֿא יִמֵּל‎ whoever does not fall down, 4:14 יִצְבֵּא דִּי לְמָן‎ to whomsoever he willeth, 4:22; 4:29; 5:21; דִי מָה‎ whatever (or simply what), 2:28 לֶהֱוֵא דִּי מָה‎ what will be, 2:29; 2:29; 2:45; Ezra 6:8; 7:18. — compare K§ 103. 2 as

mark of the Genitive, Dan 2:15 מלכא די שׁליטא‎ properly the captain, that of the king = the king's captain (a Genuine Aramaic idiom: so דְּ ᵑ7‎, Syriac constantly), 2:19; 2:25; 2:49 +? Ezra 4:15; 5:2, etc., or in the absolute state (undetermined), Dan 5:5; 7:4, 9, 10 נוּר דִּי נְהַר‎; or it may have a pleonastic suffix, 2:20 אֱלָהָא דִּי שְׁמֵהּ‎ literally his name, that of God = God's name, 2:44; 3:8, 25, 26; 4:23, etc. (so also ᵑ7‎ Syriac). To circumscribe an adjective, especially in specification of the material: 2:38 thou art דַהֲבָא דִּי רֵאשָׁה‎ the head of gold, 2:39; 3:1; 5:7, 16; Ezra 5:14; 6:4 +; as predicate Dan 2:32 טָב דִּידְֿהַב רֵאשֵׁהּ‎ his head (was) of fine gold, 2:33; 7:19; with a pronoun 2:20 wisdom and might הִיא דִּילֵֿהּ‎ are his; compare 6:27 תִתְחַבַּל דִּילָֿא וּמַלְכוּתֵהּ‎ his kingdom (is one) which shall not be destroyed, 7:14. — See further K§ 81. 3 as

conjunction (compare אֲשֶׁר‎ 8):

a. that (quod), after verbs of knowing, Dan 2:8-9, seeing 2:45; 3:27, hearing 5:14, etc.; introducing the subject of a sentence, ֗֗֗ דִּי ֗֗֗ יְדִיעַ‎ 3:18; Ezra 4:13; Dan 2:47 ֗֗֗ דִּי מִןקְֿשֹׁט‎ True is it that . . . (compare כִּי אָמְנָם‎ Job 12:2).

b. = in that, inasmuch as, whereas: Dan 2:41 and whereas (דִּי‎) thou sawest, etc. . . . it shall be adivided kingdom, 2:43; 4:20; 4:23; as a connecting link$ = seeing that, because, for (compare אֲשֶׁר‎ 8c) 2:9, 20b; 2:23b; 2:47b; 4:15; 6:24b.

c. that (ut), after verbs of asking Dan 2:16, commanding 3:10, 29, expressing a purpose 4:3; 5:15; Ezra 4:15; 6:10 +; לָא דִּי‎ that not (ne) Dan 2:18; 3:28; 6:18 (on לְמָה דִּי‎ lest Ezra 7:23, see מה‎).

d. prefixed to direct narr. (like כִּי‎ 1b, and sometimes אֲשֶׁר‎ 8a γ, and ὅτι recitativum), Dan 2:25 and said thus unto him דִּיהַֿשְׁכַּחַת‎ (that) I have found, etc., 5:7; 6:6; 6:14.

4 with prepositions and other prefixes:

a. דִי כְּ‎ (like Hebrew כַּאֲשֶׁר‎; so Egyptian Aramaic כזי‎, Palmyrene, Nabataean כדי‎, Lzb293 SACG1 62, 63 Cooke369b RES:361; כַּד ᵑ7‎, Syriac ); a according as, Dan 2:43; b. so soon as, when, 3:7; 5:20; 6:11; 6:15.

b. מִןדִּֿי‎: a. because that, Dan 3:22; Ezra 5:12 (compare מֵאֲשֶׁר‎ Isa 43:4); b. from (the time) that, after (ex quo), Dan 4:23; Ezra 4:23.

c. דִּי עַד‎ until, Dan 2:9, 34; 4:30; 7:22; = ere that 6:25.

d. דִּי עַל‎ Dan 3:19 is not a conjunction, but means above that which ...

e. for דִּי דִּבְרַת עַל‎ and דִּי כָּלקֳֿבֵל‎ see [ דִּבְרָה‎] and קֳבֵל‎.

כְּ‎ particle like, as, about (Biblical Hebrew כְּ‎, q. v.); — like, as Dan 2:40 כְּפַרְוְלָא תַּקִּיפָא‎, 4:5; 4:32; 5:1 +; according to 4:32 עָכֵד מִצְבְּיֵהּ וּכְּ‎ and according to his will he doeth, Ezra 6:9, 18 +; about (as Biblical Hebrew 1a: compare Zinjirli Lzb444 [ן‎] מלכ כשלשן‎), Dan 4:16 חֲדָה כְּשָׁעָה‎, 6:1; with infinitive (Biblical Hebrew 3b), 6:21 לִגֻבָּא מִקְרְנֵהּ וּכְ‎ and as he drew near, etc. Cpds.: — דִי כְּ‎ and כִּדְנָה‎, see דִּי‎ and דָּאנה‎; כַּחֲדָה‎; together, see חַד‎ (sub אחד‎).

דהם.def:
H1724. daham

H1726. daharah

[דַּהֲרָה‎] noun feminine rushing, dashing, of riders — Plural construct אַבִּירָיו דַּהֲרוֺת דַּהֲרוֺת‎ Judg 5:22; repetition for intensity, furious dashing.

דוגה.def:
H1729. dugah

דּוּגָה‎ noun feminine fishing, fishery, only in דּוּגָה בְּסִירוֺת וְנִשָּׂא‎ Amos 4:2 (|| בְּצִנּוֺת‎) of ׳י‎, metaphor for dragging Israel captive (compare for practice referred to, in case of fish, Ezek 29:4 & Job 40:26 scornful summons to do it with crocodile, if possible ! see Herodii. 70 on mode of capturing crocodiles).

דוד.def:
H1732. David

דָּוִיד דָּוִד,‎1066

proper name, masculine David, son of יִשַׂי‎, king of Israel, whose dynasty remained on the throne of Jerusalem till the Babylonian exile (compare 2Sam 7:11-15 etc.) (beloved one ? compare BaNB 189; according to SayceModern Rev. 1884, 158 ff.; Rel. Babylonian 53, 56 f. originally Dodo, title of sun-god worshipped in Israel compare דודה‎ name of divinity among east Jordan Israelites MI12) — דָּוִד‎ always Ruth, Samuel, Kings (except 1Kin 3:14; 11:4, 36) Psalms, Proverbs, Ecclesiastes, Isaiah, Jeremiah; also 1Chr 13:6; Ezek 34:24; 37:24-25, (c. 790 t.); דָּוִיד‎ always Zechariah, Chronicles (except 1Chr 13:6), Ezra, Nehemiah; also Amos 6:5 (where gloss according to PetersHebraica. Apr. 1886, p. 175) 9:11; Hosea 3:5; Ezek 34:23; 1Kin 3:14; 11:4, 36; Song 4:4 (c. 276 t.); — first named 1Sam 16:13; compare also Ruth 4:17, 22; 2Sam 1:1 +, 1Kin 1:1 +, 2:1 +, etc. (see above); in titles of Psalm 3-9, 11-32, 34-41, 51-65, 68-70, 86, 101, 103, 108-110, 122, 124, 131, 133, 138-145 (73 in all); also in Psalm 18:51 (= 2Sam 22:51); 2Sam 72:20; 2Sam 89:36; 2Sam 89:50; 2Sam 122:5; 2Sam 132:1132:11; 132:17; ׳ד עַבְדִּי‎ (׳י‎ speaks) 3:18; 7:5, 8 = 1Chr 17:4, 7 compare 17:26 = 17:24, also 1Kin 8:24-25, 26, 66 2Chr 6:15; 6:16; 6:17; 6:42, 1Kin 11:13; 11:32; 11:34; 11:36; 11:38; 14:8; 2Kin 8:19; 19:34 = Isa 37:35; 2Kin 20:6; compare further Psa 18:1; 36:1 (both titles compare above) 78:70; 89:4; 89:21; 132:10; 144:10; Jer 33:21-22, 26; so also as represented in coming (Messianic) ruler Ezek 34:23-24, 37:24-25, compare Hosea 3:5; Jer 30:9 (see עֶבֶד‎). Phrases are:

a. ד ׳עִיר‎ (according to SayceMod.Rev.l.c. originally city of god Dod [o]) = stronghold or citadel of Zion, 2Sam 5:7, 9 = 1Chr 11:5, 7; 2Sam 6:10, 12, 16 = 1Chr 13:13; 15:1, 29, compare Isa 22:9; especially of burial of kings 1Kin 2:10; 3:1; 8:1 2Chr 5:2; 1Kin 9:24 2Chr 8:11; 1Kin 11:27 11:43 2Chr 9:31; 1Kin 14:13; 15:8 2Chr 12:16; 2 Chronicles 13:23; 1Kin 15:24 2Chr 9:31; 1Kin 14:31; 15:8 2Chr 12:16; 2 Chronicles 13:23; 1Kin 15:24 2Chr 16:14; 1Kin 22:50 2Chr 21:1; 2Kin 8:24 2Chr 21:20; 2Kin 9:28; 2 Kings 12:22 2Chr 24:25; 2Kin 14:20; 15:7, 15:38 2Chr 27:9; 2Kin 16:20; burial of Jehoiada 2Chr 24:16; further 32:5, 30; 33:14; Neh 12:37; compare also ד חָנָה ׳קִרְיַת‎ Isa 29:1.

b. ד ׳בֵּית‎ 2Sam 3:1, 6 + (compare בַּיִת‎ 5c.

c. ד ׳אֹהֶל‎ Isa 16:5 (compare אֹהֶל‎ 2).

d. ד ׳סֻכַּת‎ Amos 9:11 (compare סֻכָּה‎ below סכך‎).

e. ד ׳כִּסֵּא‎ 2Sam 3:10 compare 1Kin 1:37; 2:12, 24, 45; Isa 9:6; Jer 17:25; 22:2, 30; 29:16; 36:30; compare 13:13; 22:4, (compare also כִּסֵּא‎).

f. ד ׳קִבְרֵי‎ Neh 3:16 compare 2Chr 32:33 בְנֵידֿ ׳קִבְרֵי‎ (compare קֶבֶר‎).

g. ד ׳מִגְדַּל‎ Song 4:4.

h. ד ׳כְּלֵישִֿׁיר האלהים אישׁ‎ Neh 12:36.

i. ד ׳אֱלֹהֵי‎ 2Kin 20:5 + (compare אֱלֹהִים‎ 4b).

j. ד ׳חַסְדֵי‎2Chr 6:42; Isa 55:3 (compare 2Sam 7:15; 1Kin 3:6; Psa 89:50; 2Chr 1:8 etc.). — (On text note the following: — דָּוִד‎ 1Sam 30:20a strike out ᵑ7 ᵐ5‎ We Dr; 2Sam 3:5 read probably name of a former husband of Eglah We Dr; 13:39 read רוּחַ‎ Wep.223 Dr; 2 Samuel 19:44 read בְּכוֺר‎ (for בדוד‎) ᵐ5‎ The We Dr; insert דָּוִד‎ 9:11; 15:32 & 24:15 ᵐ5‎ We Dr; in 1Chr 18:12; Psa 60:1 אבשׁי‎ & יואב‎ are less original than דָּוִד‎ 2Sam 8:13 We Dr).

דוה.def:
H1739. daveh

דוח.def:
H1740. duach

[דִּיחַ דּוּחַ,‎] verb rinse, cleanse away by rinsing, washing (Late Hebrew Hiph`il, Aramaic Aph`el id.; compare Assyrian dî—u DlPr 177) —

Hiph`il Perfect suffix הדיחנו‎ Kt Jer 51:34 Qr הֱדִיחָ֑נִי‎ but read הִדִּיחני‎ from נדח‎ (Hi, compare 50:17); Imperfect3masculine singular יָדִיחַ‎ Isa 4:4; 3masculine plural יָדִיחוּ‎2Chr 4:6 + Ezek 40:38 (Co conjecture הַקָּדִים‎); —

1 rinse, victims to be offered in sacrifice Ezek 40:38, Songs 2Chr 4:6 (compare above)

2 figurative cleanse by washing Isa 4:4, of removing guilt.

דוי.def:
H7495. rapha

רָפָא‎ verb heal (Late Hebrew in derivatives; Phoenician רפא‎, Syriac heal; on Aramaic proper name compounded with רפא‎ see NöZMG xi (1886), 723 Lzb369; Sabean proper name אלרפא‎ Langer1, 1 DHMZMG xxxvii (1883), 326; Arabic (and ) darn, mend, repair, pacify; Ethiopic stitch together, mend; compare KüchenmeisterZWiss. Th. xxx (1887), 257 ff.); —

Qal Perfect3masculine singular consecutive ׳וְר‎ Isa 6:10, suffix וּרְפָאָם‎ 19:22, 1singular suffix consecutive וּרְפָאתִיו‎ 57:19, etc.; Imperfect3masculine singular יִרְמָּא‎ 2Kin 20:8 +, suffix יִרְמָּאֵנוּ‎ Hosea 6:1, 1singular אֶרְמָּא‎ 14:5 +, אֶרְמָּה‎ (Ges§ 75pp) Jer 3:22; 3feminine plural תִּרְמֶּינָה‎ (Idib. qq) Job 5:18, etc.; Imperative masculine singular רְפָא‎ Num 12:13, רְפָה‎ (Idib. pp) Psa 60:4, רְפָאָ֫ה‎ 41:5, etc.; Infinitive absolute רָפוֺא‎ Isa 19:22; construct לִרְמֹּא‎ Hosea 5:13, etc.; Participle רֹפֵא‎ 2Kin 20:5 +, etc.; — heal:

1 literally,

a. of God, with accusative of person Gen 20:17 (E), Psa 107:20 (suffix), with ל‎ person Num 12:13 (JE) 2Kin 20:5, 8.
